text:
maria: ops flagged more tenant throttles that don't match abuse-detector scores. meeting notes: need clearer signal boundary between rate limiter and abuse heuristics.
kevin: current limiter only uses credit/usage and a single hard-block from detector if score>0.9. no gradual influence, so noisy detector flips can cause sudden drops.
jon: proposal: a tiny prefilter service that maps detector outputs + recent rate into a small token (bucket + soft_penalty). rate limiter reads the token from cache instead of calling detector. keeps runtime fast.
sara: Question: cache TTL tradeoffs? short TTL -> expensive detector calls, long TTL -> stale signals and fairness issues. I'd default to 5s for high-volume routes, 30s for low-volume.
maria: agreed. also we should normalize penalty by tenant baseline. a small tenant with bursty legit traffic shouldn't get the same penalty as a huge tenant.
kevin: implementation note: prefilter API returns a tiny struct. sample:```
POST /prefilter/eval
{ tenant_id, fingerprint, route, recent_tokens }
resp: { bucket: "ok"|"warn"|"block", soft_drop_p: "0.0-1.0", ttl_s: "int" }
```
jon: keep it categorical to avoid overcoupling. we'll emit the raw numeric score into telemetry for offline modeling, but limiter will only see buckets+prob.
sara: failure modes: if prefilter times out, limiter should treat as bucket=ok (fail-open) and rate-limit purely on credits. we need a kill-switch feature-flag.
maria: telemetry plan: prefilter.hit, prefilter.miss, prefilter.error, applied_soft_drop, dropped_by_prefilter, latency_p50/p95. we'll also track false_positive_rate via calibration dataset.
kevin: ops-bot: created calibration job pref-cal-20260319 to capture samples and labels every 6h for 3 days.
ops-bot: job pref-cal-20260319 scheduled; will dump to s3://redwood-pref-cal/20260319. first run in ~15m.
jon: rollout plan: feature-flag behind gateway, shadow-mode for 24h (no traffic impact) -> 1% traffic experimental with observability -> if metrics stable, ramp to 10% -> full. include A/B test pair comparing latency and false_reject.
sara: will add fairness tests in quota-sim: simulate many small tenants vs few large ones and check disproportionate drop rates. also add an integration test for TTL variance.
kevin: PR branch: infra/prefilter-cache-proto. I'll prototype in the node gateway first.
maria: one interface decision left: should we expose penalty_ms for backoff or only soft_drop probability? ms backoff more deterministic but increases coupling. leaning soft_drop only.
jon: agree on soft_drop + optional suggested_backoff field (ignored by limiter) for future use.
sara: remember to add a rolling calibration job and a daily job that compares telemetry to ground truth and warns on drift.
maria: action items: kevin -> prototype cache + feature flag; jon -> gateway client + shadow wiring; sara -> quota-sim tests + calibration checklist. I'll book 30m async sync Fri for review.
kevin: starting a draft PR and will tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
jon: will stub metrics hooks and client logic this afternoon.
sara: adding fairness scenarios now.
maria: thanks team. if pref-cal job shows weird skew, we may need to change TTLs or bucket thresholds. will reconvene after first calibration dump.
